surviving_claim: In the deterministic abstract persistence model, re-deriving cleanup residue from durable state on every restart is restart-convergent across the fixed nine-case power-loss matrix. Unsynced file-size truncation is lost, synced truncation survives, and a cleanup-complete marker durably committed before the file fsync is unsafe because it can strand stale tail after power loss.
negative_control: A durable tail-clean marker written after ftruncate but before fixed-file fsync survives modeled power loss while the file length reverts to the old durable frontier. Trusting that marker suppresses repair and strands 139264 bytes until residue is re-derived.
non_claims: this is an abstract persistence-ordering model, not a hardware power-loss test
torn sectors, drive write caches, filesystem journaling, and SQLite WAL internals are not modeled
filesystem allocated-block reclamation and device write amplification are not measured
multi-writer execution, distributed consistency, production latency, throughput, and cost are not established
